documents.content:
### 2. Site Condition Assessments (X-104, X-208, X-315)

Site assessments for all three crossings were undertaken between 4–15 November 2024. Assessments were conducted by the LCUP site engineering team with support from the RailCorp asset inspection group. The following table summarises the recorded condition entries as at 30 November 2024.

| Asset ID | Location | Condition Entry | Status | Date Assessed | Notes |
|----------|----------|-----------------|--------|---------------|-------|
| X-104 | Smithfield Road | Poor | **Current** | 12 Nov 2024 | Surface condition assessed as poor – significant cracking, edge fretting, and drainage issues at the southern approach. Basis for revised scope. |
| X-208 | Campbell Street | Fair | Current | 8 Nov 2024 | Moderate wear on crossing surface; minor alignment issues noted. Remedial works scheduled for Dec. |

The X-104 crossing upgrade has been completed and handed back to the road authority. The handback date of 27 March 2025 was achieved following early completion of outstanding landscaping works. A final site inspection was conducted on 10 April 2025, and no outstanding defects were identified.

A small number of minor items were noted during the inspection, including a loose section of fencing near the eastern approach. **3. X-315 – Signal Installation and Scheduled Upgrade**

Works on the X-315 signal installation are progressing. The signal equipment has been delivered to site and is currently being stored in a secure compound. Installation of the signal foundations is scheduled to commence on 12 May 2025, following the completion of the pre-works site inspection.

The pre-works site inspection is scheduled for 2 May 2025. The purpose of this inspection is to confirm site conditions, identify any utilities that may conflict with the proposed signal locations, and finalise the traffic management plan for the installation works. The inspection will be attended by the project team, the signal contractor, and representatives from the relevant utility authorities.

The scheduled upgrade for X-315 is currently in the detailed design phase. The design is approximately 80% complete. The remaining design work includes the finalisation of the drainage details and the development of the construction methodology for the track works. The design is expected to be completed by mid-May 2025, with construction scheduled to commence in late May 2025.

A community notification was distributed to residents and businesses in the vicinity of X-315 on 15 April 2025. The notification advised of the upcoming works and provided contact details for the project team. No concerns have been raised in response to this notification to date.

The planning phase for X-208 is progressing. The environmental assessment has been completed and submitted to the relevant authority for review. The assessment is currently awaiting approval. A response is expected by mid-May 2025.

A geotechnical investigation was undertaken at the X-208 site on 8 and 9 April 2025. The investigation included boreholes and test pits to assess soil conditions. The results of the investigation are currently being analysed. Preliminary findings indicate that the soil conditions are generally suitable for the proposed works, with some areas of soft clay that will require additional ground improvement measures.

A meeting was held with the local council on 22 April 2025 to discuss the proposed layout of the X-208 upgrade. The council raised a number of comments regarding the proposed pedestrian crossing arrangements and the location of the proposed bus stop. These comments have been incorporated into the design and an updated layout plan will be issued for council review in early May.
